analysis.paper_title: Deep Shells: Unsupervised Shape Correspondence with Optimal Transport
analysis.research_question: Can alternative optimal transport costs improve non-rigid shape correspondence?

objects.label: Equation 1
objects.title: Spectral convolution on manifold
objects.what_it_is: Defines convolution of signals F:X->R^L as pointwise multiplication in spectral space with learnable matrices.
objects.why_it_is_here: To introduce geometric deep learning background imitating CNNs on Riemannian manifolds.
objects.claim_supported: Manifold convolution can be expressed as spectral pointwise multiplication with learnable matrices.
objects.limitations: Does not establish transferability between shapes or discretization invariance; general filters are domain-dependent.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Foundational background for the spectral CNN, but not the novel contribution itself.
objects.evidence: p.2, Eq.1 and surrounding paragraph in Sec. 2.1

symbols.meaning: input signal channels on manifold X

equation.role_in_method: Background definition of spectral convolution on manifolds that the paper later smooths and truncates.

objects.research_relevance: Defines generic spectral manifold convolution, unrelated to transport cost choice for correspondence.
objects.research_relevance_reason: Background CNN theory, not OT cost.

objects.label: Equation 2
objects.title: Smooth spectral filter parameterization
objects.what_it_is: Parameterizes filter diagonals as linear combination of smooth basis functions with learnable weights.
objects.why_it_is_here: To explain how to obtain spatially localized and transferable filters despite domain-dependent eigenbasis.
objects.claim_supported: Smooth frequency-domain coefficients yield spatially localized, transferable filters.
objects.limitations: Does not specify choice of B or truncation; does not prove localization in this paper.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Key prior idea enabling the paper's smooth spectral filters.
objects.evidence: p.2, Eq.2 and following paragraph citing [15]

symbols.meaning: alternant matrix of smooth basis functions applied to eigenvalues

equation.role_in_method: Motivates use of smooth low-rank basis B for filters to achieve localization and transferability.

objects.research_relevance: Parameterizes smooth spectral filters for localization; does not involve optimal transport costs.

objects.label: Equation 3
objects.title: Product space embedding
objects.what_it_is: Embeds input shape X into R^{K+6} using intrinsic eigenfunctions plus extrinsic smoothed coordinates and normals.
objects.why_it_is_here: To set up joint extrinsic-intrinsic hierarchical matching from smooth shells [11].
objects.claim_supported: A shape can be embedded in product space of intrinsic eigenfunctions and extrinsic coordinates/normals.
objects.limitations: Does not define smoothing details; refers to [11] for construction.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Core representation of smooth shells that the deepified pipeline operates on.
objects.evidence: p.3, Eq.3 in Sec. 3.1 Product space embedding

symbols.meaning: embedding of shape X at scale k

equation.role_in_method: Defines the multi-scale product space embedding on which alignment is computed.

objects.research_relevance: Defines product embedding whose Euclidean distance becomes the ground cost used in OT matching.
objects.research_relevance_reason: Embedding defines what alternative costs measure.

objects.label: Equation 4
objects.title: Smooth shells alignment energy
objects.what_it_is: L2 alignment energy between deformed source embedding and target embedding via map P.
objects.why_it_is_here: To formalize the optimization over P and (C,tau) with increasing k.
objects.claim_supported: Shape alignment can be parameterized by functional map C and extrinsic translation tau.
objects.limitations: Non-differentiable in P due to nearest-neighbor assignment; requires good initialization.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Axiomatic energy that the paper reformulates with optimal transport to make differentiable.
objects.evidence: p.3, Eq.4 and paragraph on alternating optimization

symbols.meaning: functional map coefficients k x k

equation.role_in_method: Original smooth-shells energy jointly optimized for correspondences and deformation.

objects.research_relevance: L2 smooth-shells energy is the non-OT baseline alignment cost that the OT formulation replaces.
objects.research_relevance_reason: Baseline cost for comparison to OT cost.

objects.label: Equation 5
objects.title: Differentiable deformation update
objects.what_it_is: Defines update of deformation coefficients as argmin of energy for fixed mapping.
objects.why_it_is_here: To separate differentiable least-squares part from non-differentiable correspondence part.
objects.claim_supported: Deformation update for fixed map is differentiable linear least squares.
objects.limitations: Does not address differentiability of P-update, handled separately.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Justifies differentiability of one half of alternating scheme; minor technical step.
objects.evidence: p.4, Eq.5 in Sec. 3.2

equation.role_in_method: Shows (C,tau) step is differentiable and can stay in end-to-end network.

objects.research_relevance: Least-squares deformation update for fixed map; concerns solver step, not choice of transport cost.

objects.label: Equation 6
objects.title: Fuzzy correspondence membership
objects.what_it_is: Replaces strict point-to-point map P with probability measure pi on product domain.
objects.why_it_is_here: To make mapping from inputs to correspondences differentiable.
objects.claim_supported: Hard assignment can be replaced by fuzzy probabilistic correspondence.
objects.limitations: Alone does not define how pi is computed or regularized.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Conceptual switch enabling differentiability and Sinkhorn layer.
objects.evidence: p.4, Eq.6 and discussion of assignment matrix P

equation.role_in_method: Introduces soft correspondences to enable differentiable optimal transport formulation.

objects.research_relevance: Introduces fuzzy measure pi that allows OT formulation, prerequisite for defining any OT cost.
objects.research_relevance_reason: Foundational OT setup, not cost variant.

objects.label: Equation 7
objects.title: Marginal constraints
objects.what_it_is: Requires marginals of pi to equal surface area elements of X and Y.
objects.why_it_is_here: To define feasible set for optimal transport matching.
objects.claim_supported: Fuzzy correspondences must respect area measures as marginals.
objects.limitations: Does not include entropic regularization or cost; only constraints.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Standard OT constraints needed for Sinkhorn projections.
objects.evidence: p.4, Eq.7 defining Pi(X,Y)

equation.role_in_method: Defines OT marginal constraints for valid transport plans.

objects.research_relevance: Imposes area-measure marginals constraining feasible transports; same for any cost choice.
objects.research_relevance_reason: Generic OT constraint, not cost comparison.

objects.label: Equation 8
objects.title: Entropy-regularized OT matching energy
objects.what_it_is: OT energy integrating squared embedding distance under pi minus entropy regularization.
objects.why_it_is_here: To reformulate smooth-shells energy differentiably following [8].
objects.claim_supported: Matching energy with entropy regularization enables differentiable Sinkhorn optimization.
objects.limitations: Alignment tightness is proxy for correspondence quality; does not guarantee semantic correctness alone.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Core differentiable objective and unsupervised loss of the entire method.
objects.evidence: p.4, Eq.8 as OT reformulation of Eq.4; also used as loss in Sec.3.3 and Fig.1 caption

equation.role_in_method: Central unsupervised loss / alignment-tightness objective averaged over scales; minimized by alternating updates.

objects.research_relevance: Defines the entropy-regularized OT energy integrating squared embedding distance, the core transport cost whose alternatives would be tested.
objects.research_relevance_reason: Central OT cost formulation directly needed.

objects.label: Equation 9
objects.title: Sinkhorn alternating projection scheme
objects.what_it_is: Expresses transport density as repeated row/column normalizations of p_lambda.
objects.why_it_is_here: To efficiently and differentiably solve for correspondences pi.
objects.claim_supported: Sinkhorn iterations as alternating projections solve OT correspondence differentiably.
objects.limitations: Fixed iterations approximate exact OT; convergence rate cited from [12] not proven here.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Provides the differentiable matching layer built into network.
objects.evidence: p.5, Eq.9 and text on linear convergence and differentiability

symbols.meaning: projection onto marginal constraint of X or Y

equation.role_in_method: Differentiable update for pi_k used in hierarchical loop with fixed 10 iterations.

objects.research_relevance: Gives Sinkhorn iterations to solve OT; a solver for a given cost, not evidence about alternative costs.

objects.label: Equation 10
objects.title: Gibbs density from embedding distance
objects.what_it_is: Defines p_lambda as exponential of negative scaled squared distance.
objects.why_it_is_here: To specify Sinkhorn initialization from current deformation.
objects.claim_supported: Pairwise costs induce Gibbs distribution for Sinkhorn input.
objects.limitations: Does not include learned features; only geometric embedding distance.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Links energy cost to Sinkhorn algorithm input.
objects.evidence: p.5, Eq.10 defining input density

equation.role_in_method: Converts embedding distances to initial density for Sinkhorn.

objects.research_relevance: Defines Gibbs density from negative scaled squared distance, explicitly encoding the pairwise OT ground cost.

objects.label: Equation 11
objects.title: Truncated spectral convolution
objects.what_it_is: Defines convolution using truncated eigenbasis and low-rank smooth filter B gamma.
objects.why_it_is_here: To learn local features independent of discretization, unlike per-vertex MLPs.
objects.claim_supported: Truncated smooth spectral filters give discretization-agnostic local features.
objects.limitations: Approximates true convolution; requires choice of k, T; high frequencies truncated.
objects.paper_importance_reason: The learnable component whose output initializes matching; key to generalization.
objects.evidence: p.5, Eq.11 in Sec. 3.3; implementation details p.6

symbols.meaning: truncated spectral basis with k eigenfunctions (200 used)

equation.role_in_method: Learnable feature extractor applied to 352-dim SHOT to produce G^X, G^Y for initialization.

objects.research_relevance: Defines truncated spectral convolution for learned features; unrelated to transport cost design.

objects.label: Equation 12
objects.title: Fourier cosine basis on frequency domain
objects.what_it_is: Defines basis matrix entries as cosines of scaled eigenvalues.
objects.why_it_is_here: To provide compact smooth basis for filters operating on fixed eigen-range.
objects.claim_supported: Cosine Fourier basis on fixed frequency interval parameterizes smooth filters.
objects.limitations: Assumes 200th eigenvalue stable across surfaces; fixed interval may not hold for extreme scales.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Implementation choice for B; supports reproducibility but not central theory.
objects.evidence: p.5, Eq.12 and p.6 implementation (T=2e4)

equation.role_in_method: Concrete basis with T=2e4 used for 120 filters x 16 bases.

objects.research_relevance: Cosine basis for smooth filters; concerns feature parameterization, not OT costs.

objects.label: Equation 13
objects.title: Feature-based initialization energy
objects.what_it_is: OT energy using learned feature distance to compute initial pi.
objects.why_it_is_here: To convert refined SHOT features into starting correspondences for hierarchical alignment.
objects.claim_supported: Learned features induce initial soft correspondences via OT.
objects.limitations: Quality depends on learned features; does not guarantee global optimum.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Connects feature extractor to matching pipeline; replaces costly stochastic search.
objects.evidence: p.5, Eq.13 and Fig.1 caption describing initialization

symbols.meaning: learned local features on X and Y

equation.role_in_method: Initialization of deep shells hierarchy from learned features; replaces MCMC search.

objects.research_relevance: Defines second OT energy using learned feature distance for initialization, showing an alternative ground cost in same pipeline.

objects.label: Figure 1
objects.title: Network overview
objects.what_it_is: Diagram of full pipeline from SHOT inputs through spectral filtering to alternating pi and (tau,C) updates and textured outputs.
objects.why_it_is_here: To visualize how components interact and where loss is computed.
objects.claim_supported: End-to-end network combines SHOT, spectral filters, and hierarchical OT alignment with unsupervised alignment-tightness loss.
objects.limitations: Schematic illustration; does not quantify performance or show failure modes.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Central architectural summary linking feature learning and OT matching.
objects.evidence: p.4, Fig.1 caption and diagram showing Inputs->SHOT->Spectral Filters->Learned Features->Correspondences<->Alignment

components: Deformed shells X*_k, X*_k variations, Y_k
flow: Iterate Correspondences <-> Alignment increasing k minimizing Eq.8
Outputs + unsupervised loss as average Eq.8
figure.role_in_method: Overview of trainable pipeline and unsupervised loss computation.

objects.research_relevance: Overview shows where OT alignment energies sit in pipeline, helping locate cost modules but not comparing costs.

objects.label: Figure 2
objects.title: Inter-dataset qualitative comparison
objects.what_it_is: Texture transfer from FAUST source to SCAPE target for two baselines and ours.
objects.why_it_is_here: To show robust features on hybrid pairs lacking ground truth.
objects.claim_supported: Method yields best qualitative inter-dataset matching without postprocessing vs unsupervised baselines.
objects.limitations: Single visual example; no ground-truth metric for hybrid FAUST-SCAPE pair.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Illustrates generalization but not quantitative proof.
objects.evidence: p.6, Fig.2 with Source vs SurFMNet+icp, Unsup FMNet+pmf, Ours; FAUST->SCAPE

components: Three target color-transfer results for compared methods
flow: Source texture transfer via predicted map to SCAPE target
figure.role_in_method: Qualitative support for cross-dataset generalization claim in Table 1 last columns.

objects.research_relevance: Qualitative FAUST-SCAPE texture transfer showing overall accuracy, not alternative OT costs.

objects.label: Figure 3
objects.title: Cumulative conformal distortion
objects.what_it_is: Cumulative histograms of per-triangle conformal distortion vs other learning and axiomatic methods.
objects.why_it_is_here: To demonstrate map smoothness comparable to smooth shells despite no expensive regularization.
objects.claim_supported: Maps are as smooth (low conformal distortion) as smooth shells while more accurate.
objects.limitations: Smoothness does not imply correctness; FAUST smoother than ground-truth indicates over-smoothing possible.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Shows high-quality smooth correspondences without ARAP regularizer.
objects.evidence: p.7, Fig.3 cumulative distortion curves for FAUST and SCAPE remeshed vs baselines and ground-truth remeshing

components: Two line plots FAUST remeshed and SCAPE remeshed, x 0-2 distortion, y cumulative fraction
flow: Distortion computation per triangle to cumulative curves
figure.role_in_method: Evaluates map quality beyond mean geodesic error.

objects.research_relevance: Smoothness histograms show map quality but do not vary or evaluate transport costs.

objects.label: Figure 4
objects.title: Training set size ablation
objects.what_it_is: Plot of mean geodesic error (% diameter) vs number of SURREAL training samples.
objects.why_it_is_here: To show stability with limited training data.
objects.claim_supported: Method remains accurate with as few as 10 training shapes, unlike GeoFMNet.
objects.limitations: Only compares to GeoFMNet; single train-test setup SURREAL->FAUST.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Key data-efficiency evidence distinguishing from prior learning methods.
objects.evidence: p.7, Fig.4 geodesic error vs # training samples 10-1000 trained on SURREAL evaluated on FAUST

components: Log-x training size vs geodesic error
Three curves GeoFMNet, GeoFMNet+zo, Ours (flat low)
flow: Vary training size to test data efficiency
figure.role_in_method: Supports claim that robust OT layer helps limited data regime.

objects.research_relevance: Ablation of training size vs error; about data efficiency, not OT cost choice.

objects.label: Figure 5
objects.title: Non-isometric qualitative comparison
objects.what_it_is: Color-coded correspondence transfer to Discobolus statue scan for 7 methods.
objects.why_it_is_here: To illustrate robustness to significant deviation from training set.
objects.claim_supported: Method handles challenging non-isometric real-scan pair better than intrinsic baselines.
objects.limitations: Qualitative only; no quantitative error for this pair; weights trained on FAUST remeshed.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Demonstrates extrinsic-intrinsic advantage on non-isometric case.
objects.evidence: p.8, Fig.5 eight-panel color transfer from synthetic source to Discobolus scan

components: 7 target results: SurFMNet*, Unsup FMNet*, BCICP, ZoomOut, GeoFMNet*, Smooth Shells, Ours
flow: Same source texture mapped via each method to statue target
figure.role_in_method: Qualitative generalization to non-isometric, out-of-distribution geometry.

objects.research_relevance: Non-isometric visual comparison to baselines; no variation of OT ground cost.

objects.label: Table 1
objects.title: Matching accuracy summary
objects.what_it_is: Table of mean geodesic errors for axiomatic, supervised, unsupervised methods under 6 train-test regimes.
objects.why_it_is_here: To quantitatively compare accuracy and generalization of proposed unsupervised method.
objects.claim_supported: Unsupervised Deep Shells achieves lowest mean geodesic error on FAUST/SCAPE remeshed, including cross-dataset and joint training, beating supervised and axiomatic SOTA.
objects.limitations: Mean error hides per-pair variance and symmetry flips; remeshed benchmarks only; no statistical significance reported.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Primary quantitative proof of SOTA claim across in-dataset and generalization settings.
objects.evidence: p.6, Table 1 mean geodesic error % diameter; Ours 1.7,2.5,2.7,5.4,1.6,2.4 vs next best e.g. Smooth Shells 2.5,4.7

table.metric: mean geodesic error in % of shape diameter (sqrt area normalized, Princeton protocol)
important_comparisons: Ours 1.7 vs Smooth Shells 2.5 vs GeoFMNet+zo 1.9 (with postproc) on FAUST
Ours 2.5 vs Smooth Shells 4.7 on SCAPE
Cross-dataset F-S 2.7 and S-F 5.4 vs Unsup FMNet 9.3/12
Joint training F-F+S 1.6 and S-F+S 2.4 slight improvement
table.result_interpretation: Ours is best in all six columns without pre/postprocessing, including training on one dataset tested on other and joint training.

objects.research_relevance: Reports mean geodesic errors proving OT pipeline works but does not compare different OT costs.

objects.label: Table 2
objects.title: Runtime comparison
objects.what_it_is: Breakdown of pre, query, post and total seconds per pair for 9 methods.
objects.why_it_is_here: To show reduced query time by learning initialization instead of stochastic search.
objects.claim_supported: Method has low total test time (14s) vs axiomatic MCMC (125s) without costly postprocessing.
objects.limitations: Hardware dependence not stated; preprocessing includes 500 eigenpairs; training geodesic cost for baselines noted separately.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Supports efficiency claim: replaces stochastic MCMC search with learned init.
objects.evidence: p.8, Table 2 pre/query/post times; Ours 8.7/4.9/-/14 total vs Smooth Shells 125 etc.

table.metric: average pre-processing, query, post-processing and total time per pair in seconds at test
important_comparisons: Ours total 14s vs BCICP 881s, Smooth Shells 125s, FMNet+pmf 228s
Preproc 8.7s same as Smooth Shells; query 4.9s vs 116s; no postproc
table.result_interpretation: Large query-time reduction by removing MCMC proposals; no postprocessing needed unlike functional-map baselines.

objects.research_relevance: Compares runtime per pair across methods; irrelevant to whether alternative costs improve correspondence.

objects.title: State-of-the-art matching accuracy
objects.what_it_is: Major experimentally testable claim that method achieves best mean geodesic error.
objects.why_it_is_here: Summarizes core quantitative result justifying deepified OT pipeline.
objects.claim_supported: Unsupervised Deep Shells outperforms state-of-the-art axiomatic, supervised and unsupervised methods on FAUST and SCAPE remeshed without postprocessing.
objects.limitations: Limited to human benchmarks FAUST/SCAPE remeshed; mean error only; no test on partial or topological noise.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Central paper contribution and title claim.
objects.evidence: p.6-7, Table 1 first two columns + text Matching accuracy; Ours 1.7% and 2.5% lowest
objects.research_relevance: Claims SOTA accuracy from full system; does not isolate contribution of alternative OT costs.

objects.title: Cross-dataset generalization
objects.what_it_is: Major claim that features trained on one dataset transfer to unseen dataset/geometry.
objects.why_it_is_here: To demonstrate robustness and discretization-agnostic extrinsic-intrinsic embedding.
objects.claim_supported: Learned spectral filters generalize across datasets, to hybrid FAUST-SCAPE pairs, and to non-isometric scans, and can be jointly trained.
objects.limitations: Hybrid quantitative lacks ground truth for some pairs; qualitative examples selective.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Key differentiator vs intrinsic functional-map methods that overfit.
objects.evidence: p.6-8, Table 1 last four columns + Fig.2 inter-dataset + Fig.5 Discobolus
objects.research_relevance: Claims cross-dataset generalization of learned features, not improvement from different transport costs.

objects.title: Data efficiency and map smoothness
objects.what_it_is: Major claim combining stable few-shot training and smooth correspondences without ARAP.
objects.why_it_is_here: To show OT layer benefit and output quality beyond raw error numbers.
objects.claim_supported: Method is data-efficient (stable with 10 SURREAL shapes) and produces smooth low-distortion maps comparable to smooth shells.
objects.limitations: Data-efficiency shown only vs GeoFMNet on SURREAL->FAUST; smoothness metric does not guarantee semantic accuracy.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Supports practical utility with limited data and high-quality maps for transfer applications.
objects.evidence: p.7, Fig.4 training-size curves + Fig.3 conformal distortion overlapping smooth shells
objects.research_relevance: Claims data efficiency and low distortion maps; about training stability and smoothness, not OT cost alternatives.
